measured_on: The published answer is the four-lens blend, so materiality is measured on it. That construction DAMPENS every fork touching only the cash-flow lens by about half, and offsetting moves across lenses can cancel entirely — terminal real growth is worth 2.0% on the primary lens and 0.6% on the blend, because the same rate that lowers the discounted cash flow raises the two lenses that capitalise earnings. Nothing is hidden by that: every judgement carries its value on the primary lens alone beside its value on the blend.

judgements.name: the construction of the central
judgements.adopted: a weighted blend of four lenses at typed weights, 50/20/15/15
judgements.alternative: the cash-flow lens alone as the class primary, the other three published beside it as cross-checks
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the weights were typed and have never cleared any out-of-sample test, and three of the four lenses read this business off reported earnings, historical-cost book and a war-discounted peer group rather than valuing it; the house standard [R-LENS-03] makes the class primary the central and publishes the rest beside it. The adopted construction is both the retired one and the lower one, and it is what the delivered edition publishes, so it is recorded as adopted rather than as corrected.

judgements.name: whether the minimum top-up tax reaches the group
judgements.adopted: published BOTH ways and never averaged; the 9% audited effective rate is the branch this record is measured against
judgements.alternative: the 15% domestic minimum top-up rate as the single answer
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: 9% is the audited 2025 effective rate and 15% is the top-up that would apply if the group is consolidated into its parent for the global minimum tax; the determination has not been made about this group, so neither branch can be settled from what is disclosed, and averaging them describes a company that pays 12%, which no rule provides for.

judgements.name: the index the beta is regressed against
judgements.adopted: the FTSE ADX General index, the registered regressor for names listed on the Dubai market, beta 0.863
judgements.alternative: the DFM General index, held in the repository and deliberately not registered, beta 0.652
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the exchange resolver registers FTSE ADX General for Dubai-listed names as a LABELLED interim and the DFM General series is held unregistered, so the adopted regressor is the one the method requires rather than the one this desk preferred. It is also much the more punitive of the two, and the study prices the declined index as a full parallel valuation rather than mentioning it.

judgements.name: the weights in the cost of capital
judgements.adopted: net-debt target weights at the company policy structure, cost of debt at the facility rate
judgements.alternative: gross-debt weights, the standard textbook frame
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the company runs a stated policy leverage and pays out roughly its free cash flow to equity, so the cash pile is transient and net weights describe the structure it actually holds; the gross frame is priced rather than argued away.

judgements.name: the date the peer multiples are struck at
judgements.adopted: the subject's own anchor date, at which the primary peer closed 2.46
judgements.alternative: the earlier marks the first edition carried, at which the same peer closed 2.72
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: a relative lens compares two prices, so both must be read on the same day; the peer had fallen 9.6% between the two dates and restriking at the anchor is the like-for-like reading, which is also the lower one.

judgements.name: the cost carried on net debt
judgements.adopted: the marginal facility rate on borrowings
judgements.alternative: a blended cost of NET debt, charging the negative carry on the cash pile
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: the deposit yield sits below the borrowing rate, so netting the two raises the cost of the net position; the study discounts at the facility rate and prices the carry construction beside it.

judgements.name: whether consumption recovers or the loss is structural
judgements.adopted: published BOTH ways as equals; the recovery case is the branch this record is measured against
judgements.alternative: the continuation case, in which usage per connected tonne never recovers
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: the recovery requires a de-escalation that had not occurred at the anchor date, so the continuation case is published as an equal rather than beneath it as a sensitivity; the pass-through structure means the whole question is worth under two per cent of the answer, which is itself the finding.

judgements.name: how the related-party acquisition receivables are carried
judgements.adopted: the interest they earn is OUTSIDE operating cash flow and the balance is added at book in the bridge
judgements.alternative: the interest is capitalised INSIDE operating cash flow and no balance is added back
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: the receivables are a financial asset rather than an operating one, so capitalising their interest inside an operating multiple and then adding the principal would count them twice; carrying them at book is the cleaner treatment and, on this balance, also the lower one.

judgements.name: whether the negative working capital keeps releasing cash
judgements.adopted: net working capital held at its filed ratio to revenue, so growth keeps releasing cash
judgements.alternative: net working capital frozen at its filed absolute level, so growth releases nothing further
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: customer deposits and payment terms to the related-party supplier fund the cycle and have scaled with revenue across the filed record, so the ratio is the disclosed behaviour rather than an assumption; freezing it is the more cautious reading and is priced.

judgements.name: the age of the depreciable base the maintenance charge escalates over
judgements.alternative: the 10.29 years the notes' own cost and charge columns measure
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the measured identity returns an age only where the annual charge is cost divided by life, and the policy note states the charge is struck on cost LESS a residual, so 10.29 years overstates the age rather than measuring it; the adopted figure is an assumption, is labelled as one, and is the more punitive of the two.

judgements.name: the capital a unit of real growth is charged for
judgements.adopted: the capital intensity the business already runs at, the terminal invested capital
judgements.alternative: the marginal reading used elsewhere in this programme, which comes out NEGATIVE here
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: over these five years the existing plant is written down faster than capital expenditure replaces it and the working capital is negative and growing, so the marginal reading CREDITS the company for growing — which a chilled-water network cannot do, because another unit of demand needs another plant. The adopted reading charges more and is worth about four tenths of a per cent.

judgements.name: the real growth carried into the terminal
judgements.adopted: a fade at +0.49% real for ten years and then a perpetuity at -0.49% real
judgements.alternative: zero real growth in both stages, the house default
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: the regulated tariff carries no indexation, so nominal growth here IS volume growth and the perpetuity is a stated real DECLINE rather than a rounding of zero; on the cash-flow lens alone the adopted reading is the lower one by two per cent, and the blend muffles it because the same rate raises the two lenses that capitalise earnings.

judgements.name: the basis the equity risk premium is built on
judgements.alternative: the credit-default-swap basis, the market's own live pricing of the sovereign
judgements.direction: the study took the higher value
judgements.why: both are computed and they converge to within thirty basis points of cost of equity, which is the useful finding: on this sovereign the choice is worth about half a per cent and neither basis is doing any work.

judgements.name: the construction of the terminal
judgements.adopted: capital maintenance at replacement cost on a life derived from the audited notes
judgements.alternative: the retired form, charging reinvestment as growth over the return on capital
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the retired identity implies rebuilding the whole capital base every 1/g years — fifty in the fade and sixty-seven in the perpetuity — which is a fact about the dirham's peg rather than about a chilled-water plant the company's own notes turn over in 28.10 years. On this name the two constructions land within a fifth of a per cent of each other, which is worth recording precisely because it is the exception.

judgements.name: the size of the 2026 consumption shock
judgements.adopted: a 6% full-year fall in usage per connected tonne
judgements.alternative: the 9% fall in equivalent full-load hours the first half actually printed, carried across the full year
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the second half of 2025 was itself already soft, so the full-year fall against a full-year base is smaller than the half-on-half print. The deeper shock is worth two hundredths of a per cent and comes out marginally HIGHER, which is an artefact rather than economics: the valuation clock counts 2026 as a half-year stub, so half of that year's working-capital movement is counted and its mirror in 2027 is counted whole.

judgements.name: the basis the two-leg revenue split is struck on
judgements.adopted: the audited key-audit-matter figures, which put consumption at 56.3% of 2025 revenue
judgements.alternative: the first-half earnings deck's 49% consumption share
judgements.direction: the study took the lower value
judgements.why: the second half carries the summer cooling peak, so a full-year share always runs above a first-half share and the two are not the same measurement; the audited basis is the right one and the choice turns out to be worth a hundredth of a per cent, because the pass-through ratio moves with the split and offsets it.

unvalued.name: the disclosed control transaction
unvalued.what: the parent bought 24% at AED 2.16 in February 2026, and the study reports it as a reference point rather than as evidence of value
unvalued.why_not_valued: a related-party CONTROL price is not the same quantity as a minority fair value, so pricing "adopt it as the answer" against this model would compare two different things. It is recorded unvalued rather than guessed [R-ENF-04].

unvalued.name: the terminal maintenance basis
unvalued.what: the terminal escalates BOOK depreciation, which the shared module labels a cross-check, rather than dividing a replacement-cost capital base by the disclosed life, which it labels the standard
unvalued.why_not_valued: the standard basis needs a replacement-cost capital base and the filings disclose none; a base this desk chose is not a disclosed one (SIGCM clause 1), so the fork is named rather than filled with an invented figure.

unvalued.name: a cut to the regulated tariff cap
unvalued.what: the flat tariff underwrites the capacity charge that carries 77.9% of enterprise value into the terminal, and the model contains no machinery for a cap cut
unvalued.why_not_valued: the current instrument bars indexation of capacity charges and the achieved rate already sits at the cap, so the upward fork is settled by disclosure rather than contested; the downward one is an unmodelled risk the study names, not a choice it resolved.
